criteria.rationale: Examined the spec assumptions. Verified: the dispatch is the top-level `switch cmd` of mainCommand (cli.go:53-411); `help` is handled before that switch (cli.go:39) and exempted in the test; the 50-command floor guards the parser. Unresolved but declared: commands dispatched outside the switch are invisible to the gate. One factual slip in the known gap (`check` does have per-command help) is recorded as accepted follow-up F2.
The change is constant help text and a source-reading test; no shared state, goroutines or lifecycle are touched. The gate runs under -race in the matrix, and I re-ran it with -race: pass.
Help output only gains lines; no command, flag, file or MCP contract changes; the manual reference is additive.
No new input paths. Unknown commands still go through UnknownToken plus a help hint (cli.go:416-418); the reader change only skips deeper-indented lines.

The runtime gate in pose check (command_reference.go:96-125) keeps using helpTextEN, so instances now need the four extra reference lines, and the shipped scaffold manuals have them; I re-ran internal/scaffold: pass.
Test failures name the language, the manual path and the exact missing commands; the existing pose check message names manual and commands.

Compared the help and manual diffs: additions only, `feedback` kept as an alias and not listed twice, no dispatch change. Instances with a trimmed manual (no bash block) are still exempt (command_reference.go:113).
I ran go test ./internal/cli ./internal/scaffold (pass) and the five spec tests with -race (pass).

Root cause: the old gate (command_reference.go:16-19) treated the help as the catalog. D1 adds a gate from the dispatch read from the AST (command_catalog_parity_test.go:22-67), so the drift path is closed; D2 adds language parity, which caught the lost public-claims and the 'sem' continuation the reader misread. R5's reader change (command_reference.go:38) removes the misread at its source.

Read the manual diffs: action, issuer, migrate and release-package-manifests were added to the reference blocks of all four copies; the scaffold copies match the roots; the EN/pt-BR content exchange matches the spec's compatibility section. TestTheManualsDocumentEveryCommandTheHelpAdvertises passes.

The new help lines give a usage form and a one-line purpose for each of the 17 commands in both languages; gate failures list exact names. Typo suggestions still miss some commands (F3, accepted follow-up).
R1-R5 each map to a named test that I ran and saw pass; R3 checks EN directly and pt-BR through the parity test. Wrong comment labels are F1.
The change-set files are exactly the spec's artifact list; non-goals (per-command help, manual locale parity gate, behaviour) are untouched. Other commits in the range belong to other specs.

Static help text and a test that parses repository source and reads fixed relative manual paths; no new inputs, paths, secrets or authority. The new manual text repeats existing cross-project write constraints and adds none.

The minimal option (add 17 lines) was rejected in D1 for a concrete recurrence path; the added gate is a single 143-line test file, with no runtime registry or new abstraction. The choice is invalidated if commands come to be dispatched outside the switch, which is declared as a residual risk.

findings.action: Relabel the comments to R2 and R3 to match the spec's requirement trace.
findings.rationale: Test comments cite the wrong requirements: the language-parity test is labelled R3 (it covers R2) and the no-undispatched-command test at line 108 is labelled R4 (it covers R3).

findings.action: When doing the per-command-help follow-up, compute the missing set from the dispatch versus commandHelpCatalog instead of listing examples by hand.
findings.rationale: The known gap gives `check` as lacking per-command help, but help_catalog.go:142 defines it; the gap's example list is partly wrong.

findings.action: Add the suggestion list to the per-command-help follow-up: derive it from the dispatch, or gate it against mainSwitchCommands.
findings.rationale: knownCommandNames (the unknown-command suggestion list) comes from commandHelpCatalog, which misses dispatched commands (review-check, closeout-check, public-claims, install, amend, docs-*), so typos of them cannot be suggested; same drift class as this spec.

findings.action: Separate the description by at least two spaces (or move it to its own line) on these help lines.
findings.rationale: Help lines 504, 512 and 585 put the description one space after the command, but helpAdvertisedCommands assumes two or more; a '|' in such a description would be read as a command (caught today only by the R3 test).
